comments.text: I live on Orcas and for about 25 years. I agree with most of what is said on this video. You are either grandfathered in due to your family that got in early when it was affordable or you have to be part of a program like Opal, or in my case a program where you have to build your home, "sweat equity". The issue with vacation homes is that it's a double edged sword. On the one hand it's what fuels the economy here but then on the other hand it's what keeps people from being able to afford a home out here. There has been a lot of recent low income type housing but it only allows you to own the home not the land. Add fuel is way higher than anywhere else. Often $1.50 higher. Food is also expensive requiring a trip off island to Costco which is a all day trip and an expensive boat ride. And I agree with one commenter that wages are the lowest when you account for the cost of living. After 25 years I'm looking to move. Not because of the cost but because of the isolation. It's pretty but you are subjected to the same narrow paths you are allowed to travel so you see the exact same scenery which is beautiful but the same. You can't do anything spontaneous unless it's on the island. You can't leave without careful planning. Want to see a concert off island? Prepare to get a hotel room. And if you are off just for a day you have to plan part of your time around the ferry. You have to be there early both ways which makes for a long day much of which has nothing to do with why you are off to begin with. It's definitely a love hate relationship.
